summary: Current 1963 R-6 flattop tower in Medicine Bow NF, staffed since at least 1943 at the site, listed NHLR 1997, now a Recreation.gov rental.

facts.design: 15'x15' R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 10' concrete block base
facts.status_note: Staffed roughly 25 years then placed on standby status per NHLR; current staffing unknown

access.note: Rentable cabin via Recreation.gov; last 3 miles require high-clearance 4WD

events.note: Newspaper accounts document staffed lookout work at Blackhall, including a 16-year-old forest guard's 68-day stint
Current 15'x15' R-6 flattop tower built by Forest Service
Registered as NHLR US 229 on September 1, 1997

evidence.supports: Current tower built 1963, design and dimensions
evidence.quote: The 15’x 15’ R-6 flattop with catwalk atop a 10’ concrete block base was constructed by the Forest Service in 1963. It was used for 25 years and then put on standby status.

Nominated by
Jerry E. Schmidt, Forest Supervisor, Medicine Bow-Routt N.F.

evidence.supports: Elevation of the lookout (just over 10,900 ft)
Build year (1963, agrees with NHLR) and amenities
evidence.quote: Built in 1963, and listed on the National Historic Registry, this remote lookout tower sleeps 4 comfortably with one queen sized bed, and one twin sized bunk bed.

evidence.supports: Access road and lack of water/propane
evidence.quote: the last 3 miles leading to Blackhall Mountain Lookout require a high clearance vehicle with 4WD

evidence.supports: Still a functioning fire tower, rental can be interrupted
evidence.quote: this is a functioning fire tower and therefore availability of the cabin could be modified on the reservation system at any time to be utilized during a fire

evidence.supports: Staffing at Blackhall in 1943, youngest fire guard that summer
evidence.quote: Clay, a sophomore last year at Greeley high school, had just turned 16 years old, when he mounted to his lookout station atop Blackhall mountain, south of Encampment, Wyo., last June 21.

evidence.supports: A lookout transfer to Black Hall in 1943
evidence.quote: Ranger Williams from the Encampment area came in Monday to transfer Amos Ebersole to his new post at Black Hall lookout.

notes_for_editor: No source checked actually states a 1950 build year for the current tower; both NHLR and Recreation.gov agree on 1963, so the earlier draft's claimed 1950/1963 discrepancy was unsupported and has been removed. No clear record of when active staffing ended beyond NHLR's '25 years then standby' note, and no date given for when that standby period began.
